solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Shady event only ever seen at night

definitions.text: Shady event only ever seen at night

parts.words: Shady event only ever seen at night
parts.note: a shadowy happening that can be watched only after dark: the Earth's shadow falling across the full moon

explanation.surface: Something disreputable that only happens under cover of darkness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shady' suggests something dodgy, but here it is literal: the event is made by a shadow.
explanation.definitionFit: When the Earth's shadow covers the moon, the event is visible only from the night side of the planet.

clue.text: Light Infantry chooses to keep stone — they make up traps

parts.note: LI is the military abbreviation for Light Infantry

indicators.note: something kept is held inside, so the word for chooses goes round the stone

parts.note: to choose is to pick, so chooses gives picks
ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British unit of weight

explanation.surface: Soldiers picking out a stone to hold, and something about setting traps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Traps' is slang for mouths, and 'make up' means apply cosmetics, so the definition is about painting lips.
explanation.definitionFit: Lip colour sticks are applied to the mouth, which is slangily called a trap.

clue.text: Explosive gold, a metal that goes up!

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: OR is gold in heraldry
tin is a metal

explanation.surface: An exclamation about an explosive mix of precious and base metal rising.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for nitroglycerine, a powerful explosive liquid.

clue.text: Rummage around small sleeping-place

indicators.note: the word for rummage goes round the letter for small

parts.note: to rummage is to root about, as a pig does
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: Someone searching about for a little place to sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: A perch where birds settle down to sleep for the night.

clue.text: Cheers up in company, mostly pleasant but unresponsive

indicators.note: the reversed farewell sits inside the abbreviation for company
in a down entry, up means the farewell is written bottom to top

parts.note: ta-ta is an informal goodbye, as is cheers in Britain

indicators.note: mostly means all but the final letter of the word for pleasant

parts.note: nice means pleasant

explanation.surface: A cheerful, agreeable person in company who nonetheless fails to react.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheers' is not a toast here but the British casual goodbye, matching ta-ta; 'up' reverses it in this down light and 'mostly' trims the pleasant word.
explanation.definitionFit: A catatonic person is in a stupor, showing no reaction to anything around them.

clue.text: It's foolish restricting mother with natural expressions

indicators.note: restricting means hemming in, so the word for foolish encloses the word for mother

parts.note: idiotic means foolish
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A complaint that it is silly to hold mother back when she speaks naturally.
explanation.definitionFit: Language using the natural phrases native speakers would use is described this way.

clue.text: Disappointment about wife's bulge

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for disappointment goes round the letter for wife

parts.note: a sell is an old informal word for a letdown or swindle
W is the abbreviation for wife in genealogies

explanation.surface: A husband's dismay over his wife's expanding waistline.
explanation.definitionFit: To bulge is to swell outward; as a noun, a swell is a rounded protuberance.

clue.text: Party food prepared for a blow-out?

definitions.text: Party food prepared for a blow-out?

parts.words: Party food prepared for a blow-out?
parts.note: a blow-out sounds like a feast, but here it is candles being blown out at a celebration

explanation.surface: Catering for a big indulgent feast.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'blow-out' is slang for a lavish meal, but literally the candles on top get blown out.
explanation.definitionFit: The celebratory sponge topped with candles that the person celebrating blows out.

clue.text: Backward South American language receives new contribution

indicators.note: receives means the reversed name takes in the letter for new
backward means the language name is written right to left

parts.note: Tupi is an indigenous language of Brazil

explanation.surface: A disparaging remark about a supposedly primitive language taking on a new contribution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backward' sounds like an insult to the language but is the reversal signal: IPUT takes N inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Input is what someone puts in, their contribution to a discussion or project.

clue.text: They're alien diets forced into the one for us

indicators.note: into means the rearranged letters go inside the word for the one for us

parts.note: ours is what we call the one belonging to us

indicators.note: forced means wrenched out of shape, so the letters of diets are rearranged

explanation.surface: Foreigners pressing their strange diets onto our own way of eating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forced' does double duty in the surface as pushing food on people, but signals the anagram; 'into' is the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Outsiders are people who do not belong, strangers or aliens to a group.

clue.text: In play, thesps earwig for something the audience should hear

indicators.note: in play means set loose and moving about, so the letters are shuffled

parts.note: taken as written; thesps are actors and to earwig is to eavesdrop

explanation.surface: During a performance, actors eavesdrop on something meant for the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In play' reads as 'during a drama' but signals an anagram of THESPS EARWIG.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor's aside spoken softly but meant to carry to everyone in the theatre.

clue.text: Repayment in kind of protection given to Barnet

definitions.meaning: retaliating in the same way, blow for blow
Barnet is Cockney rhyming slang for hair (Barnet Fair); what protects it is a hat, which in the same slang is this phrase

explanation.surface: Getting your own back by repaying protection for a London borough.
explanation.walkthrough: Barnet looks like the London borough; it is rhyming slang for hair, so its protection is a hat, which rhymes with the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Equivalent retaliation, and Cockney rhyming slang for a hat.

clue.text: Whisky and soda's last in the country

parts.note: malt is a type of whisky

indicators.note: last means only the final letter of soda is used

explanation.surface: Ordering a whisky and soda while abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Malta is an island nation in the Mediterranean.

clue.text: One hundred stories to get rid of prime minister?

parts.note: de- is a prefix meaning remove, as in de-ice
David Cameron was the British prime minister when this puzzle ran

explanation.surface: A whimsical question about how many tales it takes to oust a prime minister.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'de-Cameron' as removing David Cameron, UK prime minister 2010-16.
explanation.definitionFit: Boccaccio's collection of a hundred tales told by ten people over ten days.

clue.text: Joker shortly to enter as new scoundrel

indicators.note: to enter means the shortened word goes inside the word for new

parts.note: mint means brand new, as in mint condition

indicators.note: shortly means cut short, losing the final letter

parts.note: a scream is a very funny person

explanation.surface: A prankster about to come in as the latest rogue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joker' suggests a card or a clown, but a 'scream' is a hilarious person; 'shortly' clips it before 'to enter' places it in the word for new.
explanation.definitionFit: A miscreant is a wrongdoer or villain.

clue.text: Danger originates with sons ensnaring family

indicators.note: ensnaring means trapping, so the family word is caught inside

parts.note: something that originates in a place rises there, as a river does
kin means family
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A warning that peril starts when sons entangle their relatives.
explanation.definitionFit: Riskiness is the quality of being hazardous, so it stands for peril.

clue.text: All but start of factual statement rejected figurative expression

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the letters are read in reverse
all but the start means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: a report is a factual account

explanation.surface: Plain fact is sent back in favour of metaphor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All but start of' cuts REPORT to EPORT, and 'rejected' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A trope is a figure of speech such as metaphor or irony.

clue.text: Has a debt for personal total to auditor? It increases hazardous burn rate

indicators.note: to a listener, so the phrase is heard rather than read

parts.words: Has a debt for personal total
parts.note: has a debt for is owes, personal is one (the pronoun), total is whole: owes one whole

explanation.surface: An accountant's report on a personal debt, then a warning about burning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'auditor' looks like an accountant but means a listener: OWES ONE WHOLE spoken aloud gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A thinning of the stratospheric shield lets more ultraviolet through, so sunburn happens faster.

clue.text: Completely ignoring temperature, still establishes agreements

indicators.note: completely ignoring means every occurrence of the letter is removed, not just one

parts.note: yet means still, as in yet more
sets means establishes, as in sets up
T is the abbreviation for temperature, here both of them

explanation.surface: Agreements reached without regard for temperature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Completely' means every T goes: YET + SETS loses both, leaving YE + SES.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying yes is agreeing, so the plural is a set of affirmative replies.

clue.text: Dismiss dimwit husband for rough stuff

parts.note: to sack is to dismiss from a job
a clot is a fool in British slang

explanation.surface: Firing a dim-witted spouse in favour of something coarse.
explanation.definitionFit: Coarse fabric, usually of goat hair or hemp, worn as a sign of penitence.

clue.text: Something for boring estimator losing his head

indicators.note: losing his head means the first letter is removed

parts.note: a gauger is someone who measures or estimates

explanation.surface: A dull valuer losing his head over something tedious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boring' suggests tedium, but means drilling holes.
explanation.definitionFit: A tool with a helical bit for drilling holes in wood or earth.

clue.text: Shiny surface left in view

indicators.note: in means the letter for left goes inside the word for view

parts.note: to gaze is to look at, so view gives gaze

explanation.surface: A gleaming finish left on display.
explanation.definitionFit: A glossy coating applied to pottery or pastry.

clue.text: Unorthodox train test is ruined

indicators.note: unorthodox means not following convention, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An unconventional railway trial is a disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something torn apart or wrecked beyond repair.

clue.text: Support holding side in bridge under stress?

indicators.note: holding means the word for support wraps around the bridge side

parts.note: a tee supports a golf ball
in the card game bridge, North and South are partners, one side

explanation.surface: A question about a support in a bridge under strain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bridge' is the card game, not a structure: North-South form one partnership.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone tense is anxious and strained, under stress.

clue.text: Movement from Argentina? Lack of sunlight can make it happen

definitions.meaning: a dance from Argentina, as a series of movements

definitions.text: Lack of sunlight can make it happen
definitions.meaning: without sun, a suntan will fade; read the answer as two words, tan and go

explanation.surface: An Argentine political movement thriving in the dark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Movement' suggests politics but is dance; the second half splits the answer as a sunburnt colour fading away.
explanation.definitionFit: The Argentine ballroom dance, and a phrase describing a suntan fading.

clue.text: Dash around unconvincing island battle site

indicators.note: around means the word for dash surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: elan means dash or flair
a lame excuse is an unconvincing one

explanation.surface: A dash around a feeble island to a historic battlefield.
explanation.definitionFit: The Egyptian site of decisive WWII battles in 1942.

clue.text: Take diameter from knotty rope

indicators.note: take signals removing the diameter letter
from names the word the letter is taken out of

parts.note: nodose means having knots or nodes

explanation.surface: An instruction to measure across a knotted rope.
explanation.definitionFit: A noose is a loop of rope with a running knot.

clue.text: Trial set or fixed with anybody? It might make a man of you

definitions.text: It might make a man of you

parts.note: a test is a trial

indicators.note: fixed means rigged or altered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: one means anybody, as in one never knows

explanation.surface: A rigged trial that anyone might undergo to toughen up.
explanation.definitionFit: The male sex hormone drives masculine development.
